questions.q: What does the summary say is responsible for most cases of Alzheimer's and dementia?
a: Food and lifestyle choices rather than inherited genes
A single gene passed down through families
Head injuries suffered in early childhood
A lack of mental stimulation in old age
questions.why: Lesson 1 says fewer than 1 percent of cases come from heredity, while diet and lifestyle play a much larger role.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the brain's relationship with water?
a: The brain is mostly water, which crosses the blood-brain barrier
The brain repels water to protect its cells
Water reaches the brain only through food
The brain produces all the water it needs
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the brain is about 80 percent water and that water passes the blood-brain barrier to aid energy production and flush toxins.

questions.q: Which fats does the summary say you should eat for brain health?
a: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats
Saturated fats from butter and red meat
Trans fats found in baked goods
Only fats produced inside the brain
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the brain makes its own saturated fat, so you should favor monounsaturated fats from nuts and olive oil plus omega-rich polyunsaturated fats.

questions.q: What does the summary warn about eating 25 grams of saturated fat a day?
a: It multiplies the risk of developing dementia
It improves memory but harms digestion
It has no measurable effect on the brain
It reduces the body's need for water
questions.why: Lesson 2 states that this amount of saturated fat increases the chance of dementia roughly fourfold by inflaming the body and cutting oxygen supply.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend as the best source of glucose for the brain?
a: Complex carbohydrates such as sweet potatoes and lentils
Refined sugar from sodas and candy bars
Artificial sweeteners added to coffee
Fruit juice concentrate taken daily
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to avoid refined sugar, which causes energy crashes, and choose complex carbs like whole grains, berries and sweet potatoes.
